correctness.rationale: Definitions are canonical for all n>=2; each peeling block and singleton/core flag is two-variable definable with capture-avoiding recursive unary formulas. Different signatures give separating formulas. Same signatures support a permanent two-pebble matching invariant; core/core adjacency and nonadjacency responses are available because a core vertex is neither isolated nor universal. A P4 is the smallest nonextremal core; the rational enumerator follows from a two-letter alternating-block construction. Full atlas bisimulation check through n=7 agrees for all graphs but does not replace the infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The earlier threshold-graph theorem supplies neither the handling of arbitrary graph cores nor all-graph theory counts, because a nonthreshold graph can have a nontrivial core. Conversely the core-only observation cannot distinguish arbitrary outer shell words. Together with known general games these can motivate the result, but their inspected statements do not give its full combinatorial classification and enumeration. Subsumption by uninspected general results remains possible.

value.rationale: The statement completely classifies two-variable theories of all nonempty finite simple graphs (not a contrived subfamily), shows exact invisibility of every nonextremal core, constructs minimum representatives, and gives a rational generating function for minimum-order theory counts. The classification supplies a reusable baseline for graph finite-model theory and lower bounds at larger variable widths; it is not merely a finite graph-table recomputation.
